Hettie.title: The cleverest cow
exchange: One of our cows waits until I turn away from an open gate, then slips into the lane.
How do you stop her?
I close it before fetching the feed now. She still watches for a mistake.

Hettie.title: A village breakfast
exchange: I often smell bread baking before the rest of Millwood has opened its shutters.
Who starts that early?
Anyone hoping to have breakfast ready when the household wakes. The bread does not bake itself.

Gwil.title: A crooked offcut
exchange: I keep the twisted pieces. They make the strongest little hooks.
Even the ugly ones?
Especially those. Straight wood has enough admirers.

Gwil.title: The mill at dusk
exchange: After the wheel stops, I listen for water beneath the boards.
Why then?
A loose joint makes a sound you cannot hear over a working mill.

Odo.title: Calder as a boy
exchange: Calder counted every fish twice before carrying them home.
Was he proud of his catch?
He was worried one might get away between the bank and the door.

Odo.title: The empty hook
exchange: Sometimes I cast without bait. It gives my hands a reason to be still.
Does anyone notice?
The fish, I expect. They have been very polite about it.

Tolan.title: Keeping your boots
exchange: Flour got into these boots before mud ever did.
You kept your old pair?
A wage does not make a comfortable pair grow on trees.

Tolan.title: A guard's view
exchange: From a post, you see the same person pass twice and think you know their day.
Do you?
No. That is something I try to remember before asking questions.

Serjeant Bram.title: Remembering names
exchange: I repeat a new recruit's name while checking the straps.
So you do not forget?
So the first time I say it is not when something has gone wrong.

Serjeant Bram.title: The end of a watch
exchange: I count people before I count equipment.
Even if something is missing?
A spear can wait until everyone is accounted for.

Doran.title: The least heroic skill
exchange: I can rescue porridge from a pan without scraping the burnt part into it.
That sounds useful.
It has earned me more thanks than polishing this armor.

Doran.title: Patrol weather
exchange: Rain finds the joint you thought was well covered.
Is there a trick to keeping dry?
There is a trick to packing dry socks. That is the one I know.

Elder Maddock.title: What you kept
exchange: I still have the first map I ruined in the rain.
Can you read it?
Enough to remember that certainty can wash off paper.

Elder Maddock.title: A useful question
exchange: When two travelers disagree about a road, ask when each walked it.
Which one is right?
They may both be. A flooded stream does not care what last summer's map says.

Pip.title: A beetle's manners
exchange: My guest leaves its tiny tracks all over the underside of my cap.
Does that bother you?
Only when it brings friends without telling me.

Pip.title: The sound after rain
exchange: Listen once the drops stop. The ground keeps drinking.
I cannot hear it.
Stand quietly a little longer. Even if you hear nothing, the rest is pleasant.

Mycella.title: What roots remember
exchange: A root can find the place where an old tree stood long after the trunk is gone.
Does it miss the tree?
I do not know. Finding something is not the same as knowing why you sought it.

Mycella.title: The brightest morning
exchange: Sunlight through a red cap warms every face beneath it.
Do you have a favorite spot?
The one where someone has left room for me.

Bolete.title: An inconvenient root
exchange: There is a root I move each morning. It insists the path is its bed.
Who wins?
Travelers, by daylight. The root takes the night shift.

Bolete.title: Walking gently
exchange: Small caps bend beneath a heavy step, then straighten if you give them time.
Should I stay on the path?
That would save us both some worrying.

Truffle.title: The old den
exchange: The fox left a hollow in the moss. I have never quite filled it.
Are you waiting for it?
Perhaps I am leaving a comfortable place for the next visitor.

Truffle.title: Sheltering small things
exchange: The smallest caps lean toward anything that breaks the wind.
Even you?
I am large to someone. It is a good reason to stand carefully.

The Shroom King.title: An uncomfortable crown
exchange: The crown catches on low branches. My dignity has suffered in several bushes.
Could you take it off?
I do. Nobody has yet mistaken me for less responsible.

The Shroom King.title: The quietest council
exchange: Sometimes everyone listens to the rain instead of speaking.
Does anything get decided?
Occasionally we realize the argument can wait until morning.

Calder.title: A place by the fire
exchange: I leave one dry patch for whoever arrives last.
Even if nobody comes?
Then I have a dry patch and very little to complain about.

Calder.title: Campfire stories
exchange: Travelers make a journey shorter when they tell it, and longer when they boast.
How do you tell the difference?
Ask what they ate. The truthful ones remember the disappointing meals.

Prue.title: A stone that fits
exchange: I like the moment a stone settles without rocking.
It must feel finished.
It feels ready for the next stone. Building is mostly that.

Prue.title: An old doorstep
exchange: Look at the hollow in a worn step. Years of people coming home made it.
Would you replace it?
Only when it stops carrying them safely.

Toft.title: The sound of a lamp
exchange: I check a lamp's handle before I check how brightly it burns.
Why the handle?
A fine flame is no comfort if the lamp falls from your hand.

Toft.title: Sharing a shift
exchange: Below ground, asking for help should be easier than pretending.
Was it easy for you?
No. I wish someone had told me it was allowed sooner.

Linna.title: A folded blanket
exchange: A blanket looks grand folded neatly. It feels kinder spread over cold knees.
Maren taught you that?
She handed me one before I thought to ask.

Linna.title: Market endings
exchange: The market smells different after the baskets empty.
How different?
More herbs, less bread. You can almost hear everyone planning supper.

Wren.title: The blank label
exchange: Berta once set an unlabelled jar before me during a lesson. It looked empty, but I could smell something sharp inside.
What did you say?
That I could not identify it. She said that was the correct answer until we had more evidence.

Wren.title: A patient garden
exchange: At home I sometimes wait weeks for a cutting to show new growth. I have learned to check its condition before deciding it has failed.
What do you check?
The leaves, the stem, and whether the soil is too dry or too wet. Different plants need different conditions.

Bevan.title: The smallest apple
exchange: I used to hide the little apples at the bottom of the basket.
Why did you stop?
A child asked for one that would fit in her hand.

Bevan.title: A good neighbor
exchange: A borrowed spade ought to come home clean.
Even after a long day?
Especially then. The person lending it probably had one too.

Isolde.title: A familiar bottle
exchange: I recognize my grandmother's bottle by the tiny chip beneath its neck.
You still use it?
For flowers now. Some things deserve an easier job.

Isolde.title: The last delivery
exchange: The last bottle always seems heavier than the first.
Do you charge more for it?
No. But I accept a place to sit while they find their coins.

Nazim.title: The first bucket
exchange: I check the well bucket before filling it. A loose fastening is easier to mend above the water than below it.
Did your father teach you that?
After I dropped one in. He helped retrieve it, then made me explain how it had come loose.

Nazim.title: Shade at the well
exchange: People speak more softly when they reach the shade.
From being tired?
Sometimes. Sometimes relief makes less noise than worry.

Halima.title: Tea without company
exchange: I still warm a second cup when I am alone.
Out of habit?
Out of hope. A habit need not be a bad thing.

Halima.title: Packing spices
exchange: I wrap strong spices separately. Otherwise every meal tastes like the same journey.
Even through cloth?
A little scent travels farther than you would think.

Tarek.title: An honest camel
exchange: A camel tells you plainly when it dislikes an idea.
That sounds difficult.
Less difficult than a person who agrees, then does the opposite.

Tarek.title: Listening for home
exchange: The bells sound different with sand beneath the feet and stone beneath them.
Can you tell where you are?
I can tell when the hard part of a walk has begun.

Suhaila.title: The blue thread
exchange: When I visit my daughter's workroom, I often come home with short blue threads caught in my clothes.
Do you mind finding them?
Only when I have just finished brushing myself down. They remind me of the afternoon together.

Suhaila.title: An evening seat
exchange: At the well, someone always moves a little to make room.
Even when it is crowded?
Especially then. Empty space is easy to share.

Idris.title: Three ambitions
exchange: My sons argue over whether a ship could carry a whole orchestra.
Could it?
Certainly. Whether anyone would enjoy the voyage is another matter.

Idris.title: A price remembered
exchange: People remember being embarrassed over a price longer than they remember the price.
So you bargain gently?
I try. We both have to walk through this market tomorrow.

Rashida.title: The first clear bowl
exchange: My first good bowl was plain. I watched sunlight cross it until supper went cold.
You were proud.
I had made something that let the light through without getting in its way.

Rashida.title: Sand and glass
exchange: People see finished glass and forget how ordinary its beginning looked.
Is that the secret?
Heat, care, and starting again more often than you boast about.

Bilal.title: A goat on the roof
exchange: Patience looked terribly pleased with the view.
How did you get her down?
I stopped telling her to. Curiosity did the rest.

Bilal.title: Naming the herd
exchange: Visitors think the goats all look alike until one steals their lunch.
Then they remember?
That particular goat becomes unforgettable.

Sella.title: One more bowl
exchange: I can usually stretch the stew for another person.
Without making it thin?
Bread helps. So does not making them feel they arrived too late.

Sella.title: The harbor smell
exchange: Some days I smell rain before the boats come into view.
Does that worry you?
It makes me put the kettle on. Worry ought to do something useful.

Ovid.title: The unfinished note
exchange: There is one note in my tune that sounds like a dropped hammer.
An accident?
Originally. Now everyone waits for it.

Ovid.title: The street's rhythm
exchange: A cart, a shutter, a hammer: they almost keep time together.
Almost?
A town is allowed to improvise.

Jamila.title: The lightest pack
exchange: I can tell a new traveler by how often they rearrange the same heavy bag.
What should they leave behind?
Usually the third thing they packed in case the first two failed.

Jamila.title: A familiar customer
exchange: Some people touch every jar before choosing the one they always buy.
Does that bother you?
No. A small choice can be the nicest part of a difficult day.

Nerissa.title: A dry ledger
exchange: I keep the ledger high and the wiping cloth close.
Experience?
One wave taught me that numbers can float away surprisingly fast.

Nerissa.title: The returning tide
exchange: The water covers the same stones differently each time.
Do you still watch it?
Knowing what happens next is not the same as being tired of it.

Astrid.title: The spare spoon
exchange: I keep a spoon by the door for anyone too cold to explain themselves.
No questions first?
Warm hands make better answers.

Astrid.title: A winter sound
exchange: A knock sounds small under a heavy fall of snow.
Do you listen for it?
Always when the soup is on.

Colm.title: Taking your time
exchange: I used to finish a meal before noticing whether it was good.
And now?
Now I can give the cook an honest compliment.

Colm.title: A crowded silence
exchange: People can sit together without filling every pause.
Is that awkward?
Only if someone decides it must be.

Tessa.title: A breath between notes
exchange: The breath before a tune matters. It tells people something is beginning.
Do they notice?
Their shoulders do, even when their ears have not caught up.

Tessa.title: The listener at the back
exchange: I check whether the people at the back can hear before choosing a softer passage.
How can you tell?
I ask someone, or watch for people straining to listen. Quiet music still has to reach them.

Rowan the Hunter.title: Bramble's good side
exchange: Bramble has a solemn face he wears whenever food disappears.
Does it fool you?
No. I admire the commitment.

Rowan the Hunter.title: Reading a clearing
exchange: I look for what has been eaten before looking for what I might take.
Why?
The land has mouths to feed besides mine.

Sverre.title: Dry mittens
exchange: My mother's spare mittens never matched, but they were always dry.
Did anyone complain?
Not after trying the alternative.

Sverre.title: Snow on a roof
exchange: After a heavy snowfall, I worry about the weight on older roofs. A peaceful-looking house can still need checking.
What do you look for?
New sagging or creaks. If something seems wrong, people should get clear and have the structure checked before climbing onto it.

Runa.title: Stirring the pot
exchange: Astrid lets me taste before she adds the last pinch of seasoning.
Do you agree on it?
We agree that I should stop tasting once it is ready.

Runa.title: The first puddle
exchange: After winter, I always step around the first puddle carefully.
And the second?
By the third I have accepted the mud.

Eira.title: An honest label
exchange: I label the failed batches too.
Why keep the reminder?
So I do not improve the recipe in exactly the same unfortunate way twice.

Eira.title: Autumn in a bottle
exchange: A dry autumn and a wet one leave different sweetness in the fruit.
Can everyone taste it?
They can enjoy it without naming it. That is enough.

Fenton.title: The end of a tale
exchange: I used to save the most dangerous bit for last.
What do you save now?
The part where someone had put supper aside for me.

Fenton.title: A listener's kindness
exchange: A good listener knows when a traveler is leaving something out.
Do they ask?
Sometimes they simply pour another cup.

Tallis.title: Starting together
exchange: Before a tune, I watch the other musician's hands.
Instead of their face?
Hands admit nerves sooner.

Tallis.title: A work song
exchange: A song should fit the work without making the work hurry.
Even at the forge?
Especially there. A rhyme is not worth a burned finger.

Kip.title: A useful button
exchange: I still keep that brass button.
After all this time?
It reminds me to look down sometimes. Everybody stares at the horizon.

Kip.title: The shore after a storm
exchange: The shore looks rearranged, like a room after a visitor.
Do you collect everything?
Only what I can carry without wishing I had left it there.

Ada.title: Bramble's welcome
exchange: Bramble believes every visitor came specifically to see him.
Does Rowan mind?
Rowan is usually the second to be greeted in his own house.

Ada.title: The empty chair
exchange: I mend things while I wait. It gives the waiting a shape.
Does it help?
There are fewer holes in the socks, at least.

Bren.title: A penciled question
exchange: I write questions lightly now, so an answer has room to change them.
Does Elowen approve?
She says a question is not a failure in the copying.

Bren.title: A tale's journey
exchange: A story changes a little each time someone carries it to the next town.
Does that make it false?
It makes asking where it began worthwhile.

Berta.title: A student's mistake
exchange: Wren once corrected a label I had written in a hurry.
Were you annoyed?
Briefly. Then I was very glad I had taught her to check.

Berta.title: An old routine
exchange: I still wake early even with no stall to open.
What do you do?
Enjoy a cup while it is hot. A surprisingly difficult skill to learn.

Della.title: An unruly pot
exchange: The mint keeps finding ways over the rim.
Will you move it?
I suspect it would regard a larger pot as encouragement.

Della.title: Advice about Maelis
exchange: Ask Maelis what she actually does before repeating what someone says she does.
Is she easy to talk to?
She prefers a clear question to a frightened whisper.

Ewan.title: The ordinary page
exchange: I would save a page of household accounts beside a royal speech.
Why both?
One tells you what was promised. The other may tell you what people could afford.

Ewan.title: A reader's mark
exchange: A stain on a page can mean someone cared enough to read over supper.
You do not mind the stain?
I mind people never opening the book more.

Fara.title: A box of fragments
exchange: I sort scraps by what they might become, not what they used to be.
That sounds hopeful.
It sounds untidy to everyone else.

Fara.title: A repaired cup
exchange: The ornament Sela made from Mother's broken jug still reminds me of the day I carried her the pieces.
Does that disappoint you?
No. It looks different because it has a different purpose now. Mother likes the light it catches.

Garrick.title: The apprentice's pause
exchange: That apprentice hesitates less now.
Are you pleased?
I miss knowing exactly when to complain.

Garrick.title: The lunch silence
exchange: At midday the street seems to hold its breath.
Is it peaceful?
Until somebody drops a spoon and we all hear it.

Hester.title: Starting a knot
exchange: I loosen the cord before I make a new knot.
Why loosen it first?
A knot made from an old tangle only hides the trouble.

Hester.title: A net's shape
exchange: A net needs its empty spaces as much as its cord.
I never thought of that.
Most useful things are not solid all the way through.

Junia.title: Counting coppers
exchange: I count my lamp money only once a week.
Would it not feel better every day?
It has an unfortunate habit of staying the same between repairs.

Junia.title: An evening color
exchange: Amber light makes even a plain wall look welcoming.
Is that why you chose it?
I want to enjoy coming into my own room.

Kellan.title: The rainy clock
exchange: Father's old clock is still in pieces. I kept every part together, which is more than I can say for my confidence as a clockmaker.
Will you try fixing it again?
I should ask someone who understands the mechanism before doing any more damage.

Kellan.title: Keeping a promise
exchange: A clock can tell you that you are late. It cannot make you apologize.
Do you apologize often?
More punctually than I used to arrive.

Lysa.title: A twig with wings
exchange: My newest bird has a recognizable beak.
Progress!
Yes. Now I need the rest of it to look less like a turnip.

Lysa.title: Choosing the imperfect one
exchange: The crooked glass bird catches light strangely.
In a good way?
In its own way. That was what I liked.

Cinder.title: An ember carried
exchange: I once carried a warm coal to a neighbor in a little pot.
Did it last?
Long enough for their kindling. I felt absurdly proud of the journey.

Cinder.title: A hearth's company
exchange: People stop looking at the fire once the room warms.
Do you?
I like watching something do its work without needing a word from me.

Warden.title: The squeaking wheel
exchange: Before my husband fixed his cart wheel, I could recognise its squeak from the next lane.
Did you miss the sound?
For a few evenings. A sound wheel matters more than my familiar warning that supper is due.

Warden.title: Packing something extra
exchange: A small treat fits beside the practical food.
Does he notice?
The wrapping comes home folded carefully.

Ember.title: The covered shelf
exchange: I lift the cloth when the rest of the room feels impossible.
Just to look?
To remember the dust has not claimed absolutely everything.

Ember.title: A baker's patience
exchange: The baker still shakes my coat before I enter.
After the bread argument?
He does it with a smile. That almost makes it worse.

Dagna.title: The unfinished chore
exchange: I left the polishing until morning yesterday.
Was that difficult?
I thought about it all evening. Today I am practicing thinking about something else.

Dagna.title: Fresh air's price
exchange: An open window brings dust, but it also brings voices from outside.
Is it worth opening?
Usually. A perfectly clean room can be very lonely.

Lode.title: Sleeping through work
exchange: I can sleep through hammering and wake at an unfamiliar silence.
That sounds backwards.
Familiar noise tells you someone is still there.

Lode.title: A careful shelf
exchange: I put folded cloth beneath the cup so it no longer rattles.
Does that help you sleep?
It helps the cup. I still listen for the forge.

Pike.title: A folded cloth
exchange: I wrap an extra crust separately so it is easy to offer.
Without asking?
Without making a hungry person explain.

Pike.title: The picnic place
exchange: I keep changing my mind about where that quiet picnic should be.
Have you found somewhere?
Not yet. Planning the basket is pleasant in the meantime.

Hallow.title: The jar of screws
exchange: I labelled my jar of failed hinge screws after the third repair in a month.
What does the label say?
House repairs after blasting. A plain record is more useful than another argument about whether there was any damage.

Hallow.title: A repair's first step
exchange: Before tightening anything, open and close it once.
To find the problem?
To make certain I am fixing the right one.

Quarrel.title: A useful complaint
exchange: I complained about a loose step for a week, then brought my own hammer.
Why not begin there?
Because I enjoy being right as well as useful.

Quarrel.title: A baker's truce
exchange: The baker and I can agree when a loaf is fresh.
Only then?
It is a respectable foundation for peace.

Flint.title: The morning coal
exchange: A well-banked fire leaves a little warmth waiting for you.
Even after a cold night?
Especially welcome after a cold night.

Flint.title: Hearing Quarrel
exchange: I listen for the thing underneath her complaints.
What is it usually?
Someone might get hurt. Or the bread costs too much. Both deserve a hearing.

Winnie.title: A remembered laugh
exchange: Your mother's laugh always arrived before her explanation.
Was she often in trouble?
Often enough that the laugh became useful.

Winnie.title: An old friend's visit
exchange: Nan never arrives empty-handed, even when I insist.
What does she bring?
Usually news. Occasionally more bread than either of us needs.

Ned.title: A worn strap
exchange: A pale line in leather deserves attention before it becomes a tear.
Can it be saved?
Sometimes. Looking early gives you the choice.

Ned.title: A favor remembered
exchange: I could never pay your father for helping with the cart.
Did that bother you?
Until I found someone else who needed a hand.

Nan Ferrow.title: Your muddy boots
exchange: You once tried hiding muddy boots under the clean laundry.
Did it work?
You were so pleased with the idea that you told me immediately.

Nan Ferrow.title: A place at home
exchange: I still set things where you can find them without asking.
Even while I am away?
Coming home should not require learning everything again.

Joss.title: The second hook
exchange: That hook Tam made was the first thing here that felt like mine.
More than the room?
It said I was expected to come back.

Joss.title: Packing for one winter
exchange: I packed as though a season had a fixed ending.
Does it not?
It does. Staying somewhere is another matter.

Greta.title: A familiar latch
exchange: My hand reaches for the right place before I think about the door.
You could teach someone.
I have. They always try the handle first anyway.

Greta.title: Washing in the sky
exchange: I judge a fine day by whether I can put the washing out.
Not by the warmth?
Warmth indoors is useful. Sunlight on a sheet is a pleasure.

Osric.title: Reading aloud
exchange: I still catch myself pausing where my brother used to interrupt.
What did he ask?
Whether the hero had remembered to eat. A sensible concern.

Osric.title: The cellar visitor
exchange: The traveler was disappointed by the cellar.
No lost kingdom?
A very respectable supply of ordinary things. He seemed ungrateful.

Alder.title: Waiting at a hive
exchange: I keep my hands still before I begin.
Does that calm the bees?
It calms the beekeeper. The bees appreciate the improvement.

Alder.title: Leaving enough honey
exchange: The hardest part of a good harvest is deciding what stays.
For the bees?
For the reason there will be another harvest.

Gwyneth.title: A longer scarf
exchange: Alder says the scarf could go around him twice now.
Will you stop knitting?
I am considering whether three times would be excessive.

Gwyneth.title: The warm chair
exchange: I can tell when a guest is pretending not to be cold.
How?
They keep their hands tucked away instead of reaching for the cup.

Bors.title: Even little weights
exchange: I weigh the loom weights together before sending them out.
They look identical.
Looking even and pulling evenly are different jobs.

Bors.title: The dust at the door
exchange: I leave a brush where muddy boots are most likely to stop.
Does it work?
Better than putting it where I wish the boots would stop.

Kiln.title: Opening the kiln
exchange: I still hold my breath at the first look inside.
Even now?
Experience tells you more things that might have gone wrong.

Kiln.title: The cracked bowl
exchange: An apprentice asked to throw away the old cracked bowls.
Did you let them?
No. They make useful warnings without raising their voices.

Petra.title: A small detail
exchange: I trust a traveler's account more when they remember an ordinary kindness.
Why that detail?
It is harder to borrow convincingly than a grand adventure.

Petra.title: Keeping letters
exchange: I arrange Mother's letters by the seasons she describes.
Not the dates?
Dates tell me when. Her garden tells me how it felt.

Raff.title: The chair's shadow
exchange: The shadow reaches the chair before the worst heat does.
Your father's trick?
His quietest advice. I learned it by watching him move.

Raff.title: Waiting until evening
exchange: A hard conversation is easier when nobody is hot and thirsty.
Does that solve it?
No. It removes two unnecessary arguments.

Suri.title: A hidden seam
exchange: The best seam is one the traveler never has to think about.
Do they thank you for it?
Usually only when they have owned a worse one.

Suri.title: A pocket in reach
exchange: I test a pocket while sitting as well as standing.
Why sitting?
Because roads include rests, and a coat ought to know that.

Tavin.title: The clear doorway
exchange: I check the doorway before guests arrive.
For abandoned packs?
For anything that makes arriving feel like an obstacle.

Tavin.title: Water within reach
exchange: People relax once they know they need not ask for every small thing.
You notice that?
A good welcome is mostly noticing.

Una.title: The missing towels
exchange: My sister finally returned one of the towels.
Only one?
It came wrapped around a gift. I may have lost the argument again.

Una.title: Seeds in a letter
exchange: Seeds make a letter feel heavier than it is.
With possibility?
And with my sister's certainty that I expect her to learn gardening.

Vela.title: The hidden knot
exchange: I know where every wrong-colored knot is.
Can visitors find them?
Some try. Others enjoy the rug without inspecting its mistakes.

Vela.title: A woven road
exchange: I can trace my family's route along the border without looking.
Even the wells?
Especially the wells. Those are the turns worth remembering.

Wystan.title: Reading the figures
exchange: I read a bill again after the tea is finished.
A sensible habit.
An expensive lesson can at least become a useful habit.

Wystan.title: A returning customer
exchange: I like hearing what became of something I sold.
Even if they complain?
A complaint gives me a chance to do better. Silence does not.

Rania.title: A chair outside
exchange: I carry out one extra chair before deciding who will visit.
Does someone always come?
Often enough that I keep doing it.

Rania.title: Latif's repairs
exchange: Latif has become much better at fixing chairs.
Less explaining?
The explaining is still excellent. The chairs have caught up.

Latif.title: Counting change
exchange: I still count a handful of coins twice.
Because of your mother?
Because once, the second count earned me an extra piece of fruit.

Latif.title: Stories at sunset
exchange: By sunset a small event has acquired excellent dialogue.
Do you correct the storyteller?
Only if I was in it and they gave me the dullest line.

Yara.title: The oiling day
exchange: I oil the hinges before they begin asking for it.
How do hinges ask?
Loudly, and just when everyone else is asleep.

Yara.title: A dry inland night
exchange: Inland I kept waking to listen for waves.
And heard nothing?
Nothing familiar. Quiet can be surprisingly noisy in your head.

Doryn.title: A gull's opinion
exchange: Gulls have very clear opinions about anyone carrying food.
Do you listen to them?
I keep my lunch covered. That is a form of listening.

Doryn.title: A view's price
exchange: People admire the sea through a window someone has to clean.
Is it still worth it?
Ask me after the glass dries.

Bry.title: The soup audience
exchange: Everyone remembers the soup I dropped.
Does that bother you?
Only when I carry another bowl and they all become attentive.

Bry.title: A practical doormat
exchange: The mat catches less water than I hoped.
Will you replace it?
No. It is doing its best against an entire sea.

Coral.title: Light in the window
exchange: I clean the lamp glass before dusk.
So it shines farther?
So whoever sees it knows someone has been tending it.

Coral.title: Mending that sail
exchange: I could make the patch almost invisible.
But he likes it crooked?
He likes knowing which boat is his in a crowded harbor. I can respect that.

Edda.title: The table that waited
exchange: I still notice a dry ceiling every time I sit down.
More than the table?
The roof earned its place in my affections.

Edda.title: One level chair
exchange: I have saved the rag from the old chair leg.
Why keep it?
I may need proof of how long I put up with it.

Fennel.title: The evening latch
exchange: I check the latch once, then tell myself I have checked it.
Does that help?
It gives the worrying a smaller job.

Fennel.title: A name in the garden
exchange: The fennel grows whether I am brave or frightened.
Is that comforting?
Very. It never asks me to explain myself.

Bjorn.title: A pot for tomorrow
exchange: I plan the pot around the people expected for supper, with a little extra when supplies allow.
For late visitors?
Yes. I can stretch a meal sometimes, but I cannot feed another person with an empty ladle.

Bjorn.title: Watching the table
exchange: I notice who says they have already eaten.
Do you believe them?
I offer a little anyway. Nobody has to make a speech about needing supper.

Cap.title: A shaded corner
exchange: I move my seat to leave the moss in shade.
Even if the sun is pleasant?
The moss cannot move its own chair.

Cap.title: A living store
exchange: A growing bed needs tending even when you are not hungry.
That is easy to forget.
Yes. Hunger is a poor time to begin being patient.

Ilsa.title: A loop of grass
exchange: The children tie the promise loops themselves now.
Do they remember why?
They remind me. That is how I know the lesson worked.

Ilsa.title: A season ahead
exchange: I try to picture next month's meal before taking today's shoots.
Does it make choosing harder?
It makes the choice belong to more than one hungry afternoon.

Meriel.title: An undecided customer
exchange: A customer can spend an hour choosing a cup they will hold every morning.
Do you get impatient?
I think of all those mornings. It makes an hour seem reasonable.

Meriel.title: Turning the glass
exchange: I turn the display when the light changes.
To make it shine?
To let people see what they are buying, including the little uneven parts.

Elin.title: A narrow sunbeam
exchange: The sun reaches my kitchen table for only a short while.
So you move the table?
Sometimes breakfast follows the light across the room.

Elin.title: Something beautiful
exchange: I used to think a useful purchase had to look plain. Now I wonder whether enjoying something each morning is useful too.
Are you thinking of the glass flower?
Yes. I have not bought it yet, but it has made me reconsider what I expect from a purchase.

Maelis.title: A grateful goose
exchange: The goose never thanked me when its wing healed.
Would you have expected it to?
No. People are the ones who make gratitude complicated.

Maelis.title: A clear question
exchange: Bring me what you actually saw, not what the village has decided it means.
Even if it sounds foolish?
Especially then. Embellishment is harder to work with than foolishness.

Archivist Elowen.title: The quiet visitor
exchange: I notice who opens a book and then looks around before reading.
Why?
Sometimes they need to know they are allowed to ask the question inside it.

Archivist Elowen.title: A missing name
exchange: A gap in a record is worth investigating. It might be damage, an omission, or somebody deliberately removing a name.
How do you tell which?
Compare copies and inspect the page. The gap asks a question; it does not answer it for us.

Mira.title: A careful drawing
exchange: I mark uncertain details lightly on my sketches.
So you can erase them?
So nobody mistakes my best guess for a measured wall.

Mira.title: Letters from miners
exchange: A letter may describe supper beside an account of danger.
Does that make it less useful?
It makes the writer a person, which the official report often forgets.

Oren.title: Closing the book
exchange: I put frightening accounts away before sunset now.
Does it stop the dreams?
Not always. It makes room for another thought before bed.

Oren.title: Names on stones
exchange: I copy names carefully when I study the dead.
More carefully than the dates?
Both matter. A name is not simply a decoration above a number.

Tamsin.title: The tree-door story
exchange: I have finally decided what is behind the door.
Will you tell me?
An ordinary kitchen. I want to know why that feels more surprising than a monster.

Tamsin.title: The torn cushion
exchange: I repaired the cushion but left a small patch showing.
So you can recognize it?
So everyone else can too. I have defended that chair for years.

Master Iven.title: A pupil's correction
exchange: The finest lesson sometimes begins with a pupil saying I have made a mistake.
You like that?
I like when they can show me why. That means they were thinking.

Master Iven.title: Maps and people
exchange: A map marks towns neatly, but a town is never just its center.
What is missing?
Gardens, errands, and the reasons someone chooses to stay.

Brin.title: Measuring a stair
exchange: I have drawn a little scale along the edge of my notebook.
For the temple steps?
For anything people insist is too large or too steep to describe properly.

Brin.title: A doorway in a sketch
exchange: If two accounts disagree about a door, I draw both in light lines.
Until you visit?
Until evidence gives me a reason to darken one.

Nell.title: Saying the whole name
exchange: I still take a breath before saying Halvard's name in class.
Are you afraid?
Sometimes. I say it anyway, at an ordinary volume.

Nell.title: Who paid the price
exchange: I ask whose home a grand decision reached first.
Why the first home?
Because someone always lived where the official account begins.

Sable.title: The copied mistake
exchange: A misspelling can show how one book borrowed from another.
An error can help?
If you notice it instead of copying it again.

Sable.title: Changing your mind
exchange: I leave enough room in my notes to disagree with myself later.
Does that happen often?
Often enough to justify the paper.

Pella.title: The globe's edge
exchange: I can turn the globe until the coast faces the window.
What do you imagine?
That the light on the paint is sunlight on actual water.

Pella.title: A first journey
exchange: I do not need my first journey to be heroic.
What would you like?
To arrive, look around, and have enough time before coming home.

Bess.title: The chipped cup
exchange: I retired a chipped cup from serving drinks and kept it for measuring dry supplies behind the counter.
Why keep that one?
I knew its capacity and it could still do that job safely. It was no longer suitable for someone's mouth.

Bess.title: A room settling down
exchange: I know the moment a noisy room becomes a comfortable one.
How?
People stop speaking over the person who has just arrived.

Ronan.title: The late apple
exchange: I check the late-ripening tree even when everyone says it has failed.
Out of loyalty?
Out of experience. Patience is easier after you have tasted the reason.

Ronan.title: A clean barrel
exchange: Making good cider includes a great deal of cleaning nobody sings about.
Should Ovid write a verse?
Only if it helps with the scrubbing.

Venn.title: A letter's weight
exchange: A folded page weighs almost nothing until you know someone is waiting for it.
Do you read them?
Only when I am asked. Carrying a story is different from owning it.

Venn.title: Finding the reader
exchange: I learned to ask whether someone wants a letter read quietly.
Why quietly?
Not every piece of news belongs to the room.

Hobb.title: The fourth leg
exchange: I have cut the fourth leg for the chair I am building at home. It still needs fitting and checking.
Will it stand evenly?
That is the next test. I am not inviting anyone to sit until the joints are sound.

Hobb.title: Moving a table
exchange: Everyone carrying a table believes their end is the difficult one.
Which end is?
The one discovering the doorway is narrower than promised.

Edric.title: The thing you left
exchange: I miss fewer things from my old heavy pack than I expected.
What do you miss most?
The confidence that carrying everything gave me. My shoulders do not miss it.

Edric.title: A day without a story
exchange: An ordinary evening feels especially good after a troublesome road.
What makes it good?
Dry feet and nobody shouting my name.

Dorr.title: A useful nap
exchange: I wake before a cup has gone completely cold.
How do you manage that?
Years of practice. I would not want to appear careless.

Dorr.title: The dawn habit
exchange: Sometimes I wake early and decide the wagons can unload themselves in my memory.
Can they?
Beautifully. They have had years to learn.

Ser Anwen.title: A mended strap
exchange: I still check the stable straps when I visit.
Even after becoming a knight?
A title should not make your hands forget useful work.

Ser Anwen.title: An oath in plain words
exchange: I prefer an oath a frightened person can understand.
Why them?
They are the ones who need to know what I promised.

Grusk.title: Measuring doors
exchange: I still turn sideways near a narrow doorway, even without a barrel.
A habit?
My shoulder remembers the width of work.

Grusk.title: An honest deck
exchange: I count the cards before Dain begins explaining the rules.
Does he object?
He calls it a lack of trust. I call it arithmetic.

Fen.title: The first step
exchange: I watch a new dancer's shoulders before their feet.
What do they tell you?
Whether they need a lesson or permission to enjoy themselves.

Fen.title: Entering a room
exchange: I am getting better at looking for a familiar face instead of an exit.
Is that a change?
A small one that feels quite large from inside.

Senn.title: A cheerful loss
exchange: I practice losing a small wager without spoiling everyone's evening.
Is that practice necessary?
Some people are astonishingly bad at it.

Senn.title: The folded hand
exchange: Knowing when to fold means noticing the cards instead of your pride.
Can you separate them?
Not always. That is why I keep the wagers small.

Dain.title: A swept floor
exchange: You learn a great deal about travelers from what falls out of their boots.
Useful for wagers?
Useful for sweeping. The wagers came later.

Dain.title: Explaining the rules
exchange: Nyra insists I explain all the rules before we begin.
A terrible burden.
You understand my difficulties better than she does.

Rusk.title: The piece of paper
exchange: I keep my daughter's address wrapped against rain.
You must know it by heart.
I do. Carrying it is for a different kind of remembering.

Rusk.title: A voice in fog
exchange: The man who talked through the pass kept me from feeling alone.
Did you thank him?
After we were through. I had spent the first half wishing he would stop.

Linnet.title: A tune without words
exchange: Different people tell me the same tune reminds them of different homes.
Which is it about?
Whichever home they need to hear that evening.

Linnet.title: The remembered hum
exchange: I remember my grandmother's humming more clearly than most of her songs.
Why that?
She hummed when she was not trying to perform for anyone.

Puck.title: Practicing quietly
exchange: I have learned to practice the difficult part more softly.
For Bess?
For everyone who has already heard me fail at it.

Puck.title: A song of your own
exchange: It still feels strange when someone recognizes my tune.
Good strange?
Very. I try not to grin until they have finished listening.

Vale.title: A hat in a doorway
exchange: I remove the hat before passing through narrow doors now.
Experience?
Architecture is an unforgiving critic of fashion.

Vale.title: An unremarkable story
exchange: I would like to tell a story that makes nobody ask for another.
Could you?
I have had a very ordinary breakfast. I can describe it at length.

Cerys.title: An honest question
exchange: My sister brings questions home that stay at the table through supper.
Do you answer them?
I add questions of my own. We eat before solving the world.

Cerys.title: Losing at cards
exchange: I now understand why I lose some hands.
Does that make it better?
It makes the other losses more irritatingly mysterious.

Nyra.title: Watching the audience
exchange: A conjurer watches the audience as closely as the audience watches him.
For suspicion?
For the instant they begin enjoying themselves.

Nyra.title: A fair surprise
exchange: I like being surprised when nobody loses something important.
Even by Dain?
Dain could surprise me by dealing the same number of cards to everyone.

Maren.title: A towel first
exchange: A wet traveler often apologizes before asking for a room.
What do you say?
That the floor has been wet before and survived.

Maren.title: A well-made bed
exchange: I smooth the sheet where tired feet will find it.
Does anyone notice?
Comfort does not need to announce which small kindness made it.

Dunstan.title: An honest fit
exchange: I would rather hear that the armor pinches before you leave the shop.
Even after all the work?
Especially then. Good work includes listening to the person wearing it.

Dunstan.title: The blade above the bench
exchange: That bent first sword keeps me from claiming I was born knowing the trade.
Do apprentices ask about it?
The brave ones. I like them immediately.

Sela.title: A held breath
exchange: People hold their breath when they watch hot glass take shape.
Do you?
I have work to do. I breathe and let them worry for me.

Sela.title: A useful imperfection
exchange: A bubble can catch the light in a way a perfect pane never will.
So every mistake is useful?
No. Recognizing which ones are useful is part of learning.

Tam.title: The old press
exchange: The press turns smoothly now, but Joss still pauses at the stubborn part.
Out of habit?
Out of respect for two afternoons with a wrench.

Tam.title: Returning a kindness
exchange: Nan will not let me repay the soup.
What will you do?
Find a reason she ought to take something home. We are both stubborn.

Celia.title: The last page
exchange: The blank page at the back of my notebook has become rather important.
Even with nothing on it?
It means I have not decided I am finished learning.

Celia.title: The laundry list
exchange: I kept a copy of that ordinary list beside the battle account.
Why?
Somebody expected to have clothes worth washing after the fighting.

Ivo.title: A box that closes
exchange: The lid now closes if you press the left corner first.
Does that count?
As progress, yes. As finished, Grandfather would have had opinions.

Ivo.title: Tools at rest
exchange: I clean the tools even on days I do not use them.
Why?
It keeps tomorrow's work from beginning with yesterday's neglect.

Merrin.title: The spare place
exchange: I move the spare cup away from the table's edge before I sit.
Expecting company?
Making room for it. There is a difference.

Merrin.title: Watching the lane
exchange: Some footsteps make me look up before I know why.
Your brother's?
Sometimes only the way I remember them.

Zella.title: The smallest hole
exchange: A little tear is easier to mend before you can put your hand through it.
That seems obvious.
Most useful lessons do, once somebody has taught them to you.

Zella.title: A length of cord
exchange: I never cut the spare cord until I know how much is needed.
To save it?
To avoid discovering I was generous with the wrong end.

Iris.title: Wood before weather
exchange: I bring the dry wood close while the door still opens easily.
Before the frost?
Before I can use the frost as an excuse for not doing it.

Iris.title: A visitor's errand
exchange: I keep tea ready for neighbors with suspiciously small errands.
Do they know you know?
I hope they know they are welcome. That is the useful part.

Alderic.title: A swept threshold
exchange: I sweep even when I expect no visitor.
For the temple?
For the person who may arrive while I expect nobody.

Alderic.title: The old carvings
exchange: In the old rider carvings I have studied, the hands tell as much as the weapons.
What should I notice?
Whether they are reaching, holding, or helping. Those gestures survived too.

King Halvard.title: The silent room
exchange: People used to interrupt me. Now they wait until I have finished.
Does that tell you they agree?
It tells me they have learned when to speak.

King Halvard.title: What remains of trust
exchange: Trust cannot hold a kingdom together when everyone wants something different.
Can fear?
Fear has never failed to make itself understood.

Cartwright Oswin.title: The spare peg
exchange: I always carry a spare peg for the wheel.
But the wheel still broke.
A spare peg is excellent protection against one very particular misfortune.

Cartwright Oswin.title: A turn in the road
exchange: A cart makes you notice corners people on foot walk around without thinking.
Is that why you know the roads?
I know the corners. The roads connect them.

Miner Marn.title: Another stone badger
exchange: I made a bird from a chip last night.
Did Nerik recognize it?
He said it was a badger looking upward. I kept it anyway.

Miner Marn.title: Listening to stone
exchange: A loose stone sometimes shifts before it falls.
Can you hear it?
If nobody is shouting over the person who noticed.

Miner Nerik.title: The lamp at home
exchange: Mother still says the old lamp was perfectly good.
Does she use the new one?
Every evening. She is very consistent about both things.

Miner Nerik.title: Two pairs of hands
exchange: Marn and I work faster when we agree which stone moves first.
Instead of both pulling?
Two people hurrying in different directions are just another obstacle.

Snowbuilder Nessa.title: The loose hat
exchange: I leave the little snow figure's hat at a jaunty angle.
Why that angle?
It looks as though it has just thought of something.

Snowbuilder Nessa.title: A thawing face
exchange: I do not mind when the snow faces begin to change.
After all the work?
A winter decoration is allowed to enjoy the spring.

Orin.title: A place to pause
exchange: I like a spot where I can watch people arrive without blocking their way.
Why there?
A welcome should not become another thing to get past.

Orin.title: Recognizing footsteps
exchange: Some neighbors have a pace I recognize before I see their faces.
Mine too?
Yours often sounds as though a question is pulling it along.

Weft.title: A patient thread
exchange: I smooth a thread before trying to pass it through a narrow eye.
Does that help?
More than becoming cross with something thinner than a hair.

Weft.title: A useful scrap
exchange: I save small pieces until I know what they can mend.
Do they pile up?
Everything has to earn its drawer eventually.

Dorrick.title: A pause for supper
exchange: I try to put work down before the meal goes cold.
Try?
There is always one last thing. It has remarkable stamina.

Dorrick.title: A sound repair
exchange: I trust something mended carefully more than something new that nobody has tested.
Why?
The repair tells me somebody noticed where it failed.

Hask.title: An ordinary visit
exchange: It is pleasant when someone stops without needing an urgent favor.
Am I interrupting?
Only the usual thoughts. They can wait a moment.

Hask.title: The familiar road
exchange: A familiar road changes slowly enough that you stop noticing.
What makes you notice?
Walking it beside someone seeing it for the first time.

Garrow.title: A job finished
exchange: I like setting the tools in order after a job.
More than the work?
It is the part that tells my hands they may stop.

Garrow.title: A helpful question
exchange: Asking where to put something is more useful than guessing.
Even when the answer seems obvious?
Especially if somebody else has to find it later.

Marek.title: An unhurried cup
exchange: I prefer a cup I can finish without standing up halfway through.
A rare luxury?
Common enough to forget it is pleasant.

Marek.title: Recognizing a face
exchange: I remember people better than the things they bought.
Does that help with business?
It helps with being glad to see them again.

Bregga.title: Preparing early
exchange: I put things within reach before the weather makes reaching difficult.
Does it save much trouble?
It makes a cold morning ask less of me.

Bregga.title: An open door
exchange: A doorway loses its warmth quickly when somebody stands there talking.
A hint for me?
An invitation to decide whether you are coming in.

Torvald.title: A lamp's glass
exchange: A clean lamp glass gives the flame a fair chance.
Is that the first thing you check?
After checking that the person carrying it knows where they are going.

Torvald.title: Packing for darkness
exchange: I put things in the same pockets before going somewhere dark.
So you can find them?
So a small need does not become a long search.

Ingrid.title: A winter routine
exchange: I check the latch before settling beside the warmth.
Every night?
Habits are useful when tiredness is trying to make decisions.

Ingrid.title: A neighbor's window
exchange: A lit window can make a cold lane feel less empty.
Even if you do not go in?
Knowing someone is there can be enough.

Sigrun.title: The spare wrapping
exchange: I keep a dry piece of cloth for unexpected weather.
Does it get used?
Often enough that unexpected is an optimistic word.

Sigrun.title: Waiting out the cold
exchange: There is no shame in taking a little longer when the footing is poor.
Do people forget?
Usually the ones most eager to tell you how quickly they arrived.

Asta.title: A comfortable seat
exchange: I choose a seat by how long I would happily remain in it.
Not by the view?
A fine view loses charm when your back begins complaining.

Asta.title: An evening's company
exchange: A conversation need not become memorable to be worthwhile.
What makes it worthwhile?
Going home a little less alone than when you arrived.
